title: Rethinking Full Arch: Expanding the Fixed Treatment Menu
html:
Full-arch dentistry continues to evolve, yet many patients who need comprehensive treatment still leave practices without receiving fixed care. Dentistry Today spoke with Dale Spadafora, DMD, chief clinical officer of Stabili-Teeth, about why he believes full-arch dentistry has reached an inflection point and why the next evolution may be about expanding, rather than replacing, existing treatment modalities.

Q: What do you see as the biggest opportunity in full-arch dentistry today?

Dale Spadafora (DS): We have excellent full-arch solutions. I perform them and believe in them. But I’ve also watched too many patients who need treatment and want fixed teeth leave without moving forward. Sometimes the barrier is anatomical, sometimes financial, and sometimes both. Often, the alternative becomes a removable denture or overdenture.

Stabili-Teeth set out to address that gap: Can we create another predictable, fixed, non-patient-removable option for appropriately selected patients without compromising the quality of the treatment?

Q: How is the Stabili-Teeth clinical approach different?

DS: Stabili-Teeth is a patented, fully implant-supported full-arch protocol utilizing 6 implants, incorporating standard and true narrow-diameter implants.

That combination allows us to strategically utilize available native anatomy in ways that can expand candidacy for certain patients. The 6-implant design provides distributed retention and cross-arch stability, while the prosthesis is fixed for the patient and retrievable by the clinician. The protocol is designed to provide patients with fixed provisional teeth the day of surgery, followed by the definitive prosthesis after healing.

It’s also a defined surgical and prosthetic workflow with training, protocols, implant and laboratory partners, rather than pieces a dentist has to assemble into a system.

Q: How can Stabili-Teeth offer fixed treatment at less than half the price of many traditional All-on-X treatments without compromising quality?

DS: The economics aren’t created by discounting dentistry or substituting inferior components. They’re created through the process.

Stabili-Teeth has a standardized national pricing model, strategic implant and laboratory partnerships, and a patented workflow designed around efficiency and predictability. We use high-quality implant, attachment, and prosthetic components.

The patient isn’t receiving a “budget version” of fixed full-arch treatment. It’s a different pathway to an implant-supported, fixed restoration, typically at less than half the patient price of traditional All-on-X treatment.

Q: Why do practices need another fixed option?

DS: Look at the automobile industry. One manufacturer doesn’t make one vehicle at one price for every consumer. There are different models for different needs.

Dentistry already operates this way. We have different implant sizes, restorative materials, and treatment modalities. Full-arch shouldn’t be the exception. Adding another modality doesn’t diminish what you’re already providing. It expands the patients you’re capable of helping.

Q: Stabili-Teeth also emphasizes the business side. Why?

DS: Because being clinically capable of treating more patients only matters if those patients make it into treatment.

Stabili-Teeth was built as more than a clinical protocol. The platform includes professional education and clinical support, but also patient acquisition, marketing, lead engagement, financing resources, consultation training, team education and an on-demand Academy.

We’ve thought through the journey from first inquiry through consultation, treatment, and final teeth, giving practices a pathway rather than asking them to build every piece themselves.

Q: What would you say to an experienced All-on-X doctor?

DS: Don’t replace it. Expand the menu.

Full-arch is increasingly competitive. Instead of simply spending more to compete for the same patients, look at those already calling your practice and sitting in your consultation room. How many need you, want fixed teeth, and are still leaving untreated?

If we can expand clinical candidacy, financial qualification, and the infrastructure supporting treatment, we’re not simply competing for more full-arch patients. We’re expanding the full-arch market itself.
